content: Baylor College of Dentistry (BCD), located in East Dallas, Texas, serves as the dental education unit of the Texas A&M University System and is a component of the Texas A&M Health Science Center. Approximately two-thirds of all dentists in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex received their education at BCD, and over one-third of all dentists in Texas are alumni of the college. It is the largest single provider of oral healthcare services in the Dallas/Fort Worth metropolitan area. The college was established 100 years ago as the State Dental College, beginning with an initial class of 45 students. Today, it has an enrollment of approximately 520 students and boasts over 8,000 graduates. BCD is internationally recognized for its excellence in oral health sciences education, research, specialized patient care, and community service programs. The college offers degrees in dental hygiene, graduate training in dental specialties, and a Ph.D. program in biomedical sciences. It also provides post-doctoral degrees in dental specialties and collaborates with Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center in Lubbock for its D.D.S. program. Baylor College of Dentistry has been named one of the top four dental institutions in the United States for periodontology, endodontics, and geriatric dentistry by American Health Magazine. In 1997, through its Center for TeleHealth, BCD became the first dental school in the nation to successfully demonstrate the use of telecommunications technology for dental medicine. This was achieved through a long-distance patient consultation between dentists at the BCD campus and 175 dental professionals gathered in Orlando, Florida. Each year, the college completes over 103,500 patient care visits, with 45% of these services benefiting low-income individuals. This amounts to approximately $3 million in community services annually. Additionally, BCD produces the nation’s only syndicated, weekly dental health news program, Dental Health Check. The college also provides continuing education opportunities for dental professionals worldwide, allowing them to access the latest advancements in dental technology. In terms of research, BCD is a nationally recognized center for oral health education and both basic and clinical research. Faculty members are pioneering advancements in areas such as laser technology, computer-aided dental restorations, dental material improvements, craniofacial deformity treatments, and salivary dysfunction therapies. Furthermore, research conducted at BCD extends beyond dental medicine, addressing the prevention and treatment of diseases such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, cancer, and diabetes. The college is centrally located in Dallas, just one mile east of the downtown business district and adjacent to Baylor University Medical Center. Faculty members also oversee dental clinics at two local children’s hospitals and provide oral healthcare services to the Parkland Health & Hospital System, the Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Dallas, Baylor University Medical Center, and Denton State School.
